name: Lindsey Graham
role: U.S. Senator from South Carolina (2003-2026); U.S. Representative (1995-2003)
summary: A conservative Republican and prominent defense and foreign-policy hawk who backed the Iraq war, NATO, Ukraine and Israel and urged force against Iran. He opposed the Affordable Care Act, sponsored federal abortion limits and favored tax cuts and balanced-budget rules, while occasionally working with Democrats on immigration reform. He became a close ally of Donald Trump after criticizing him in 2016.

sources.usedFor: Saved wiki-policy.json, wiki-foreign.json and wiki-economy.json; dated record, not interest-group scores.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted against the Affordable Care Act in 2009 and 2010 and authored the 2017 Graham-Cassidy plan, which would have returned health-care decisions to the states.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Argued in 2015 that raising the minimum wage makes hiring harder.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Backed the 2017 corporate rate cut and phasing out the estate tax; in 2015 he favored closing loopholes and means-testing, not higher rates on the wealthy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His 2026 speech promises enforceable civil liability for social-media harms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Supported maintaining FISA surveillance of terrorism suspects (2015) and monitoring Islamic websites; defended NSA programs as aimed at terror suspects.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Supported medical marijuana but opposed recreational legalization (2020); called for a war on fentanyl (2022).

limit-guns.rationale: Held an A rating from the NRA, opposed expanding background checks and backed concealed-carry reciprocity; he did back a limited 2022 package with red-flag provisions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Proposed a defense-spending floor of 4% of GDP (2007) and backed funding for more ICE agents (2025).

traditional-family.rationale: Stated support for traditional families and used the tax code to reinforce them (1994, 2014).

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for DOMA and supported a federal marriage amendment; later accepted the Obergefell ruling but said states should decide and voted against the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022.

abortion-legal.rationale: Sponsored federal abortion limits (20 weeks in 2015, 15 weeks in 2022, with exceptions for rape, incest and the mother's life) and criticized Trump in 2024 for not backing a federal limit.

more-religion-public.rationale: Supported school-prayer legislation and a school-prayer constitutional amendment (1997, 2001).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His victory speech praises inherited traditions and remembering what makes the country great.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He explicitly favors increasing legal immigration to meet workforce needs, while demanding border enforcement.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Supported the NATO-led intervention in Libya and urged action on Syria.

open-borders.rationale: Supported more ICE agents, a southern border emergency declaration and changes to asylum law; never advocated open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Mixed, leaning against: he backed emissions reductions and co-wrote a 2009-10 climate bill, but called the Green New Deal crazy and opposed EPA greenhouse-gas regulation and economically disruptive measures.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He urges building and completing nuclear reactors and personally defends construction tax credits.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Supported phasing out the estate tax (2001).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Backed protecting the steel industry from Chinese dumping (2018) and supported tariffs on national-security grounds; Cato described his record as mostly protectionist.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He champions targeted tax incentives to secure nuclear construction and research capacity.

democracy-best.rationale: He insists elections must proceed even when his party might lose, rejecting suggestions of cancellation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Mixed: he supported a constitutional amendment on school prayer but defends non-establishment alongside public faith.

military-superiority.rationale: Longtime defense hawk who pushed a 4% of GDP defense floor and supported a large military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Durbin recounts Graham explicitly telling Trump America is defined by ideals rather than race or color.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: He introduces legislation requiring providers to enable government decryption under judicial warrants.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He says politics should improve lives and find cross-party agreement when useful, while retaining conservative principles.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expressed support in 2026 for annexing Greenland and backed assertive US power abroad.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Among the Senate's strongest supporters of Israel; backed recognizing Jerusalem as its capital and weapons for Israel.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Backed a balanced budget amendment and Cut-Cap-and-Balance, but also voted for a $900 billion COVID relief package in 2020.

force-without-un.rationale: Voted for the 2002 Iraq resolution, urged a preemptive strike on Iran (2010) and force against Maduro (2019), without calling for UN approval.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Supported opening the Outer Continental Shelf to oil and gas leasing (2008) and opposed EPA greenhouse-gas rules.

consent-of-governed.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

separated-powers.rationale: He defends judicial limits but backs presidential war without prior congressional authorization.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authored a 2005 amendment limiting habeas corpus for detainees and backed a border emergency, though he opposed torture; position is mixed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Supported US wars and defense strength; no sign of support for this position.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Supported NATO and allied commitments; said "America First" is not isolationism (2026).

death-penalty.rationale: Called for an effective death penalty (1994) and backed capital punishment for child rapists (2008).

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Favored abstinence-based sex education over contraception (2014) and sponsored abstinence education funding.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Suggested in 2010 amending the 14th Amendment to end birthright citizenship.

collective-defense.rationale: Strong supporter of NATO and its enlargement to Ukraine and Georgia (2008).

women-must-cover.rationale: He condemns compulsory veiling enforced through killings and surveillance in Iran.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He expressly accepts adverse election judgments despite his personal disagreement, rejecting unilateral reversal.

elective-rulers.rationale: He defends choosing the president through the constitutional election count rather than a vice president’s personal decision.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Proposed personal retirement accounts within Social Security in 2000, but said in 2015 he wanted to save the program as is.

single-official-language.rationale: Supported declaring English the official language of the United States (1999).

non-intervention.rationale: Repeatedly urged intervention abroad (Iraq, Libya, Venezuela, Iran, Afghanistan presence).

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Career defense hawk and Air Force reserve colonel who pushed for higher military spending.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Backed NATO, Ukraine and Israel against rival powers; no neutrality advocated.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: his explicit rejection of racial definitions of American membership implies opposition to racially restricted citizenship’s political rights.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He argues postwar Iraq requires a coalition and loose confederal arrangement among Sunnis, Shias and Kurds.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Supported funding welfare through religious and community nonprofits (2000).

recognise-genocide.rationale: Briefly blocked then voted for the Senate resolution recognizing the Armenian genocide in 2019.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Supported the Iraq war, called for preemptive action against Iran and force against Venezuela.

arms-reduction.rationale: Voted against ratifying New START (2010) and sought high defense spending.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Military hawk and veteran who backed many foreign wars; nothing suggests support for refusing orders.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Backed a balanced budget amendment (2009) and the Cut-Cap-and-Balance Pledge (2012).

voter-id.rationale: His 2026 victory speech demands identification and citizen-only voting requirements.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Supports sanctioning ICC action against Israeli leaders.

close-ties-china.rationale: Took a confrontational line on China trade and Taiwan, and backed tariffs on buyers of Russian oil including China.

notes:
Not living: died 11 July 2026 (s1, s4). Only directly documented positions are answered; no inferences beyond the low-confidence items. Views shifted over time: supported comprehensive immigration reform in 2006-2013 and stronger border enforcement later; criticized Trump in 2016 and became an ally from 2017.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 22 answers taken from it, 18 agreed, 2 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent third-model audit; full blank list and all active statements reviewed. Prior notes and sources were read, but no previous answers. The ten prioritized items yield revolution-justified, consent-of-governed, ethnic-nation, democracy-best and elective-rulers. Natural rulers, monarchy, national rebirth, hereditary-title abolition and the small armed vanguard theory remain null: support for Pahlavi does not itself endorse monarchy, and mass uprisings are not foco theory. The single historical inference is explicitly labelled and low confidence. Election consent is contested because two witnesses describe the Georgia call differently from Graham; the allegation is not treated as judicially established. Constitutional checks are mixed in light of his expansive war-power position rather than automatically generalized from January 6. His bipartisan compromise rhetoric does not erase conservative commitments or imply that left and right are obsolete. New primary research includes lengthy foreign-policy interviews, Senate speeches, campaign captions, an encryption bill and minimum-wage hearing. His final-year programme is distinguished from later memorials: Durbin’s account is secondhand and medium confidence. The religious-school curriculum question remains null; support for public prayer is not religious instruction. Ordinary public faith and a prohibition on religious establishment are distinct. No view is inferred simply from Baptist identity. His support for modest wage adjustments does not cancel opposition to the substantial $15 proposal. Aid framed as a national-security instrument is not an asserted worldwide duty to give substantial aid. Fossil expansion and nuclear support coexist with qualified emissions reduction. Later explicit positions take precedence over earlier rhetoric. No score is derived from animal-welfare ratings or from the views of other AI-hearing participants. Nonconsensual deepfake liability does not establish a position on all pornography or on automating government. General all-drug legalization, broad AI optimism, human enhancement and the more specialized economic doctrines remain unknown.
